doc.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018

title: Borrowed tubas, his mother's savings and practicing in the projects
summary: He borrowed tubas until his mother's savings bought his first after college; neighbors came to enjoy his playing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: When did you get your own tuba?

Oh yeah well that’s a very interesting story. I borrowed tubas until I graduated from college. I just didn’t have the financial means to buy an instrument. So many band directors, they realized that I couldn’t, so they would just like lend me the tuba and said I can use it until, as long as I returned it when I was done. And what happened, when I graduated from college, my mother, unbeknownst to me, she was, all this time she would just say, because that’s the way, my mother was one of those people that she would just save money. She’d put a penny here, a dollar there. So all through this period my mother was saving money, saving money, saving money, until when I graduated from college she had enough money that she gave me the payment to be able to buy my first, because I bought my first tuba after I graduated from college at Manhattan School of Music nonetheless.
Logistically I just think of you like carting a tuba home on the school bus or whatever.

Oh yeah, I did that, oh yes, I did that. I mean at that time I mean you just loved to play an instrument so much you didn’t care. But those were heavy. But you didn’t care. You just put it on the train and you know, get down there and lug it up the stairs, and then you know my neighbors told me — we lived in the projects in New York City and of course everybody is very very close together. So my neighbor said the first time that I played a tuba in the apartment man they didn’t know what was going on, they thought maybe an elephant had escaped, the sound was so horrendous. And my mother, she was just like, “Oh my God what is he doing?” Oh man. So she just ran in the room, “Are you okay?”
“No, Mom, that’s how it’s supposed to sound.”

Yeah. But then, you know, I practiced every day. And my neighbors, because you know the neighbors in New York, they’ll just start knocking on the wall. But my neighbors, they realized that, you know, they knew my family and they knew that I was trying to get someplace in life.
This was a good pursuit for you.
Yeah, this was a good pursuit. Yeah. So they didn’t bother me. And after a while, you know, they began to enjoy what I was playing. Melodies were actually coming out. Things they could recognize.
